name: ai.edgechat/edgepedia
title: Edgepedia
description: Search and read Edgepedia, a free and growing encyclopedia with citations. No key.

tools.name: search
tools.description: Search an encyclopedia for facts about a person, place, thing, event, or concept: Edgepedia, more than 500,000 articles with citations. Pass the subject's name ("Mount Fuji", "photosynthesis"), not a question; other names and misspellings match, and when no title matches, articles whose text does follow, marked `match: fulltext`. Returns results with id, title, url, and preview text, plus a `topic:` result when the query names a topic ("painters"); pass an id to `fetch`. `limit` and `page` reach further results.

query.description: The name of a subject, or words from an article title.

topic.description: Only articles under this topic id (as `fetch` topic:… names it, without "topic:").

tools.name: fetch
tools.description: Read an encyclopedia article in full: one Edgepedia article as Markdown with its citations, by a `search` result's id. Returns id, title, text, url, and metadata (topic path, license, credit). A `topic:` id lists that topic's parent, narrower topics, and articles, 120 a page; `topic:root` is the top of the tree, `topic:geo` the geography tree. `citations: false` gives [n] markers instead of inline source links. Show the `credit` line with any text you quote.

id.description: The id of a search result (the last part of the article's address, such as "mount-fuji", or a topic's "topic:…" id).

citations.description: Default true. false = [n] markers instead of inline source links; the numbered reference list stays.

page.description: A topic only: which page of its articles, from 1.

ids.description: More ids to fetch with `id` in one call, up to 10 in all.

section.description: Only this section, by its heading ("Etymology", "History").

outline.description: true = add the list of the article's headings.

max_tokens.description: Cut the text at a section boundary to about this many tokens; pass `next_cursor` as `cursor` for the rest.

cursor.description: Where to continue, from a cut text's `next_cursor`.

length.description: snippet or lead for a short text; full (default) for the whole article.

format.description: The text as plain text, HTML, JSON-LD, or Turtle instead of Markdown.

tables.description: true = add the article's tables as JSON and CSV.

chunks.description: true = the text as paragraphs with stable ids, in `chunks`.

query.description: Only the 3 passages that best match these words, each with a `cite_url`.

quote.description: A sentence from the article, or a chunk id: adds a `cite_url` that opens the page at it.

cite.description: Add a reference in this format (csl, bibtex, ris, apa, mla, chicago, harvard).

links.description: Add the articles linking here (in), the links it makes (out), or both.

links_page.description: With links "in" or "both": which 30 articles linking here, from 1.

lang.description: The article in this language, by its code ("es", "zh"): the translation when one is stored; otherwise the English, with how to have it translated.

tools.name: related
tools.description: Find encyclopedia articles related to an Edgepedia article: its topic-mates, a few from each neighboring topic, and its geography neighbors. Pass its id, as for `fetch`. Returns groups of results; `fetch` a group's `topic` id for more.

id.description: An article's id, as `search` returns it (such as "mount-fuji").

by.description: "links" = articles cited together with it, and articles linking to what it links to.

tools.name: connect
tools.description: Find the shortest chain of in-text links from one Edgepedia article to another (at most 6 hops), with the sentence that makes each hop; pass two ids as `search` returns them.

from.description: The starting article's id (such as "koala"), its ep… id, or its title.

to.description: The target article, named the same ways.

tools.name: resolve
tools.description: Find which encyclopedia article a name means: Edgepedia's best match for a person, place, thing, or concept named in a text, with a confidence, whether the name is ambiguous, and the alternatives. Pass the name ("Mercury"), and optionally words from the text around it (`context`: "planet orbit") or a topic id the article must sit under (`type`). Returns `result` (id, title, url) and `alternatives`; pass an id to `fetch`.

name.description: The name as the text gives it.

context.description: Words from the text around the name, which favor the article they fit.

type.description: Only articles under this topic id (as `fetch` topic:… names it, without "topic:").
